transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I’ll finish one thing at school or at home, and then I immediately jump into the next thing. It feels like I can’t really shut myself off.
Lately, have you been needing less sleep than usual?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that I need less sleep, exactly. I mean, my sleep can feel off sometimes, but I don’t think I’m suddenly sleeping way less and feeling fine or anything like that.
Do you get distracted easily?
I’m not sure. I mean, I can lose track of things sometimes, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether I’m getting distracted more than usual.
Did this feeling of being constantly driven start all of a sudden, as a clear change from your usual self?

No, I don’t think it started all of a sudden. This has kind of been me for as long as I can remember. My mother used to joke that in elementary school I was basically teaching the class from my seat because I was always out of my chair, talking, or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So it doesn’t feel like some brand-new change in who I am.
Has being this restless or always on the go caused problems for you at school, work, or in relationships?

Yes. At work it’s become a real problem. The complaints have gotten serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan. And at home, my spouse says the caregiving routines are harder because people have to manage my energy on top of everything else.

I don’t mean to cause problems—I’m usually trying to help—but I feel like I’m damaging trust with my colleagues and my family.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention in class or finishing schoolwork?

I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear memory of whether I had trouble paying attention in class or finishing schoolwork. I remember being very active in class, but the schoolwork part is harder for me to say.
Does this happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?

Yes, it definitely happens in more than one setting. At work, it’s serious enough that I’m on a corrective plan because of complaints. And at home, my spouse says our caregiving routines are harder because people have to manage my energy too. I’m trying to help, but it feels like I’m wearing down trust with both my colleagues and my family.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
I’m not sure I’d say that. I do worry about things, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed myself spending a lot of time worrying about a bunch of different things all the time.
Did these problems begin after a particularly stressful event or major life change?
Yes, I think so. This level of trouble has been going on for about eight months, since our older relative moved in with us. That was the big change I can point to.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that as the main problem, at least not in a clear way. I’d have to think about it more, but I can’t say for sure that I often lose focus in conversations or tasks.
Before age 12, were you already often restless or always on the go?

Yes, definitely. My mother used to joke that in elementary school I was practically “teaching the class” from my seat. I was always out of my chair, talking, or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So yeah, that was there long before adulthood, not just something that started with the family change.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

Yes. I do that a lot. I’ll jump into conversations with colleagues or parents, or at home between my spouse and our relative, because I think I’m helping or moving things along. But I end up talking over people or taking charge before they’ve even finished what they were trying to say.
Since your relative moved in, have you felt unusually overwhelmed by that situation?

I’m not sure I’d call it unusually overwhelmed. It’s been a lot to adjust to, sure, but I don’t know that I can separate that out clearly or say it’s the main issue. I’d need to think about what you mean by overwhelmed.
Since your relative moved in, have you been having more conflict than usual because of that situation?

Yes, there’s been more conflict. At home, my spouse says the caregiving routines are harder because everyone is having to manage my energy on top of everything else. And at work, it’s gotten serious too — complaints got to the point where I was put on a corrective plan. I feel like I’m damaging trust with both my family and colleagues, even though I’m trying to help.
Since your relative moved in, have you felt more distressed than you think most people would in that situation?
I’m not sure. I mean, it’s stressful, but I don’t really know how to compare my reaction to what most people would feel. I haven’t thought of it that way.
Since your relative moved in, have you felt that this situation has been hard to adjust to?

I’m not really sure. It’s been an adjustment, yes, but I don’t know if I’d say that’s the thing that’s been hard in a clear way. I can tell it changed the household, but I haven’t sorted out how much of what I’m feeling is because of that specifically.
Before your relative moved in, were these same problems already causing noticeable trouble in your life?

Yes. This goes way back. My mother used to joke that even in elementary school I was practically teaching the class from my seat because I was always out of my chair, talking, or cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, no, this didn’t just start when my relative moved in. It’s been part of how I’ve been for a long time.
